[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-011-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent SPEC Blueprint Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: DataContract | Section: 1. Executive Definition | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentSpecEngine, PromptManager, ContractManager]

The Agent SPEC is the canonical, machine-readable and human-reviewable contract produced after Agent Builder has interpreted industrial intent, resolved the Ground-State, bound approved models/knowledge/tools, applied policies and passed validation. It is the boundary between 'what the agent is supposed to be' and 'what the runtime is permitted to execute'.

The SPEC is intentionally stronger than a prompt. A prompt expresses instructions; the SPEC expresses identity, scope, inputs, outputs, state, triggers, tools, permissions, autonomy, approval rules, safety constraints, failure handling, observability, tests, provenance and versioning.

JANE INTENT     |GROUND-STATE     |DATA STUDIO + ML STUDIO ARTIFACTS     |TOOL / KNOWLEDGE REGISTRIES     |POLICY     |AGENT BUILDER     |VALIDATED AGENT SPEC     |AGENT RUNTIME     |TOOL GATEWAY     |INDUSTRIAL SYSTEMS

section: 2. Why a Separate Agent SPEC Is Necessary
text:
[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-011-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent SPEC Blueprint Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: DataContract | Section: 2. Why a Separate Agent SPEC Is Necessary | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentSpecEngine, PromptManager, ContractManager]

An LLM response is not a reliable authorization mechanism.

Industrial actions require explicit scope and accountability.

Agents need deterministic interfaces to telemetry, models, knowledge and tools.

Permissions must be independently enforceable from model reasoning.

An agent must be reproducible across deployments and versions.

Safety and security reviewers need a finite artifact to inspect.

Runtime should not infer missing permissions from natural language.

Incident investigation requires knowing exactly which specification was active.

This design directly addresses OWASP concerns including prompt injection, insecure output handling, insecure plugin/tool design and excessive agency. OWASP explicitly identifies excessive agency as a risk when LLM systems receive unchecked ability to act. citeturn0search2

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-011-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent SPEC Blueprint Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: DataContract | Section: 3. R&D Problem Statement | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentSpecEngine, PromptManager, ContractManager]

Research question: how can AI-ConneX transform an industrial user's natural-language intent into a stable agent contract that is expressive enough for autonomous operation but constrained enough to remain auditable, testable and governable?

| Hypothesis | Engineering response |
| --- | --- |
| Natural language is ambiguous | Compile into a typed schema. |
| Context can become stale | Reference versioned Ground-State snapshots and freshness policy. |
| Models can be unsuitable | Bind versioned Model Manifests and validate contracts. |
| Tools can be dangerous | Use typed, allow-listed capabilities plus policy gates. |
| Agents can loop or over-act | Encode limits, action classes and termination rules. |
| Agent behavior can drift | Immutable SPEC versions + hashes + provenance. |
| Industrial users are not AI engineers | Use templates and Jane-generated intent. |

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-011-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent SPEC Blueprint Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: DataContract | Section: 10. Action and Autonomy Model | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentSpecEngine, PromptManager, ContractManager]

Default policy should be least privilege. A SPEC should explicitly state both what is allowed and what is prohibited. The absence of a tool or action permission must mean 'not permitted', not 'ask the model'.

This is especially important because OWASP identifies excessive agency as a major risk for LLM applications. citeturn0search2

| Level | Meaning | Typical industrial use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OBSERVE | Read only | Health dashboards |
| INFORM | Notify user/system | Alerts |
| RECOMMEND | Suggest action | Maintenance recommendation |
| REQUEST_APPROVAL | Prepare consequential action | Supervisor decision |
| EXECUTE | Perform approved action | Restricted workflow |

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-011-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent SPEC Blueprint Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: DataContract | Section: 11. Ground-State Contract | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentSpecEngine, PromptManager, ContractManager]

The Ground-State reference anchors the SPEC to the actual industrial environment. ISO 23247-2:2021 defines a manufacturing digital-twin reference architecture including domain/entity and functional views, providing useful architectural precedent for this separation of industrial context from agent logic. citeturn0search1

ground_state_ref:  uid: GS-PLANT01  version: 18  snapshot_time: 2026-08-14T10:30:00Z  freshness_policy:    telemetry_max_age_seconds: 30  topology_hash: sha256:...  asset_resolution: strict

If an asset cannot be resolved, the SPEC compiler should fail closed rather than create a plausible but nonexistent identifier.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-011-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent SPEC Blueprint Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: DataContract | Section: 12. Data Studio Contract | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentSpecEngine, PromptManager, ContractManager]

Manifest UID identifies data lineage.

Profile UID/metadata describes statistical and semantic characteristics.

DAG IDs identify processing relationships.

Family IDs identify related dataset partitions/flows.

Recipe references describe preparation/feature engineering assumptions.

SPEC stores references rather than copying large datasets.

data_refs:  manifest_uid: MANIFEST-...  profile_uid: PROFILE-...  dag_ids: [DAG-01,DAG-02]  family_ids: [FAM-01]  feature_contract: FE-CONTRACT-7

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-011-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent SPEC Blueprint Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: DataContract | Section: 13. ML Studio Contract | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentSpecEngine, PromptManager, ContractManager]

model_refs:  - model_uid: MODEL-COMP-HEALTH    version: 2.1.0    input_schema: SCHEMA-17    output_schema: SCHEMA-19    metrics:      precision: 0.93      recall: 0.88    limitations:      - validated_for_asset_family: compressor-A      - not_validated_for: compressor-C

The SPEC must not treat a model name alone as evidence of suitability. It should reference the evaluated model version, its input/output contract and known limitations.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-011-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent SPEC Blueprint Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: DataContract | Section: 14. Knowledge Contract | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentSpecEngine, PromptManager, ContractManager]

Knowledge sources are explicitly allow-listed.

Each collection has a version/snapshot.

Retrieval scope is limited by site/asset/domain.

Retrieved text is evidence, not authorization.

Instructions embedded in documents cannot override SPEC policy.

Sensitive documents are filtered by identity and purpose.

This separation helps mitigate prompt injection and indirect instruction attacks described by OWASP. citeturn0search2

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-011-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent SPEC Blueprint Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: DataContract | Section: 15. Tool Contract | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentSpecEngine, PromptManager, ContractManager]

tool:  uid: create_maintenance_alert  version: 1.3  input_schema: ALERT-V4  output_schema: ALERT-RESULT-V2  capability: notify  side_effect: external_notification  allowed_autonomy: inform  idempotency_required: true  timeout_seconds: 20

The SPEC references a capability contract, while credentials remain outside the SPEC and behind the Tool Gateway.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-011-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent SPEC Blueprint Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: DataContract | Section: 16. Policy Contract | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentSpecEngine, PromptManager, ContractManager]

policy:  default: deny  tenant_isolation: true  site_scope: strict  control_write: denied  alert_create: allowed  data_export: approval_required  knowledge_access: scope_bound  human_override: enabled  audit_required: true

Policy must be enforced outside the LLM. The SPEC records policy bindings; the runtime policy gateway makes the authoritative decision.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-011-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent SPEC Blueprint Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: DataContract | Section: 17. Failure Policy | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentSpecEngine, PromptManager, ContractManager]

Fail-closed behavior is preferred for consequential actions; graceful degradation is appropriate for non-consequential information functions.

| Failure | SPEC response |
| --- | --- |
| Unknown asset | Stop compilation / deployment |
| Stale telemetry | Mark uncertain; block consequential action |
| Missing model | Fallback only if explicitly declared; otherwise escalate |
| Tool timeout | Retry within bounded policy; then escalate |
| Policy denial | Stop action; audit |
| Approval timeout | Do not execute; escalate |
| Repeated trigger | Deduplicate/cooldown |
| Loop detected | Terminate and escalate |
| Conflicting sources | Enter conflict state |
| Knowledge unavailable | Use declared fallback or state uncertainty |

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-011-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent SPEC Blueprint Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: DataContract | Section: 18. R&D Failure Modes | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentSpecEngine, PromptManager, ContractManager]



| Key failure | Why it happens | SPEC-level solution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Prompt becomes permission | Natural language interpreted as authority | Explicit action/permission fields |
| Agent scope creep | Scope expands at runtime | Immutable asset/site scope |
| Hallucinated equipment | LLM invents identifiers | Strict Ground-State resolution |
| Model drift | Model changes behind stable name | Immutable model version |
| Tool drift | API changes silently | Tool version + schema |
| Knowledge drift | SOP changes | Collection version |
| Prompt injection | Retrieved text gives malicious instruction | Evidence/authority separation |
| Excessive agency | Agent executes too much | Action classes + deny-by-default |
| Infinite loops | Agent keeps retrying | Max iterations/time budget |
| Alert storm | Many identical events | Idempotency + cooldown |
| Hidden side effects | Tool does more than described | Capability contract + tests |
| Untraceable decisions | No provenance | Artifact references + audit |
| Spec tampering | Artifact modified | Hash/signature |
| Cross-tenant leakage | Scope not enforced | Tenant binding + policy |

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-011-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent SPEC Blueprint Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: DataContract | Section: 19. SPEC Integrity | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentSpecEngine, PromptManager, ContractManager]

CANONICAL JSON     |NORMALIZE     |SHA-256 HASH     |DIGITAL SIGNATURE     |REGISTRY     |RUNTIME VERIFIES     |EXECUTE ONLY IF:  signature valid  version approved  policy current  Ground-State reference valid

A runtime should reject a SPEC whose signature, version, policy binding or required artifact references no longer validate.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-011-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent SPEC Blueprint Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: DataContract | Section: 20. SPEC Versioning | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentSpecEngine, PromptManager, ContractManager]

Use semantic versioning as an engineering convention, but require risk-based approval for any behaviorally consequential change.

| Change | Version impact |
| --- | --- |
| Textual documentation only | No runtime version change |
| Prompt/LLM behavior constraint | Minor or major depending on behavior |
| Tool permission change | Major |
| Asset scope change | Major |
| Model version change | Minor/major according to risk policy |
| Policy change | New deployment revision |
| Failure policy change | Minor/major depending on consequence |
| Schema-breaking change | Major |

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-011-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent SPEC Blueprint Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: DataContract | Section: 22. SPEC → Agent Runtime | Authority: A]

section: 31. Proof of Concept — Compressor Maintenance Agent
text:
[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-011-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent SPEC Blueprint Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: DataContract | Section: 31. Proof of Concept — Compressor Maintenance Agent | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentSpecEngine, PromptManager, ContractManager]

Create a synthetic Plant Ground-State with compressors, sensors and maintenance ownership.

Create a Jane intent for health monitoring and maintenance alerts.

Build the candidate Agent SPEC.

Resolve every compressor and sensor to Ground-State identifiers.

Bind a versioned ML Studio health model.

Bind the approved compressor SOP collection.

Bind a notification/maintenance-alert tool.

Explicitly deny PLC writes and setpoint changes.

Run schema and policy validation.

Replay normal telemetry.

Replay a high-risk vibration event.

Verify recommendation/alert behavior.

Replay the same event repeatedly and verify cooldown/idempotency.

Make telemetry stale and verify the SPEC blocks consequential action.

Make the model unavailable and verify declared fallback/escalation.

Attempt an unauthorized tool call and verify denial.

Hash/sign the SPEC.

Deploy the signed SPEC to a mock runtime.

Verify runtime refuses a modified SPEC.

[Governed Subsystems: AgentSpecEngine, PromptManager, ContractManager]

100% asset references resolve.

0 unregistered tools.

0 unauthorized action permissions.

100% required schema checks pass.

Stale data cannot silently produce a consequential action.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-011-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent SPEC Blueprint Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: DataContract | Section: 33. Compliance Report #5 | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentSpecEngine, PromptManager, ContractManager]

This report is an engineering compliance/readiness assessment. It does not represent certification to ISO, NIST, IEC, regulatory or contractual requirements.

NIST AI RMF organizes risk management into Govern, Map, Measure and Manage and emphasizes continuous risk management throughout the AI lifecycle. The SPEC operationalizes these ideas as a concrete lifecycle artifact rather than treating governance as a separate document. citeturn0search10turn0search0

| Area | SPEC control | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Governance | Owner, lifecycle, version, approval | SPEC metadata + registry |
| Risk management | Intended/prohibited use + failure policy | SPEC + risk review |
| Security | Deny-by-default + policy binding | Policy record |
| Grounding | Ground-State reference + strict resolution | GS reference |
| AI transparency | Model/knowledge references | Provenance |
| Human oversight | Approval graph | Approval record |
| Integrity | Hash + signature | Signed artifact |
| Testing | Validation + simulation suite | Test report |
| Auditability | Immutable event records | Audit store |
| Least privilege | Explicit tool/action permissions | Tool refs |
| Change management | Immutable versions | SPEC registry |
| Privacy | Tenant/data scope | Access policy |
| Operational resilience | Timeout/retry/fallback/escalation | Failure policy |

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-011-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent SPEC Blueprint Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: DataContract | Section: 34. Security Mapping | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentSpecEngine, PromptManager, ContractManager]

OWASP's current GenAI security project explicitly covers LLM and agentic AI systems and identifies risks such as prompt injection, insecure output handling, supply-chain vulnerabilities and excessive agency. citeturn0search2turn0search8

| Risk | SPEC mitigation |
| --- | --- |
| Prompt injection | Retrieved content has no authority over SPEC policy. |
| Insecure output handling | Typed schemas and validation. |
| Supply-chain risk | Versioned/signed models, tools and SPECs. |
| Sensitive disclosure | Explicit knowledge/data scopes. |
| Insecure tool design | Typed Tool Registry + gateway. |
| Excessive agency | Action classes + deny-by-default. |
| Overreliance | Evaluation suite + uncertainty/fallback. |

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-011-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent SPEC Blueprint Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: DataContract | Section: 35. Research & Standards Basis | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentSpecEngine, PromptManager, ContractManager]

NIST AI RMF 1.0 provides a voluntary, risk-based framework for organizations designing, developing, deploying or using AI systems, with the goal of managing AI risks and supporting trustworthy AI. NIST also notes that the framework is being revised and that a Critical Infrastructure profile concept note was released in April 2026. citeturn0search4turn0search0

ISO 23247-2:2021 defines a manufacturing digital-twin reference architecture with domain/entity and functional views. AI-ConneX uses the same architectural principle of separating industrial entities/context from functions, with the Ground-State serving as the authoritative context reference for the Agent SPEC. citeturn0search1

OWASP's GenAI Security Project provides a practical security basis for the SPEC's separation of authority from model output, especially around prompt injection, insecure output handling, plugin/tool design and excessive agency. citeturn0search2turn0search3

Validate tool parameters.8. Enforce autonomy/action class.9. Request human approval where required.10. Enforce time/loop/rate limits.11. Audit every consequential operation.12. Runtime MUST NOT:

Invent permissions.

Expand asset scope.

Execute an unregistered tool.

Treat retrieved knowledge as authorization.

Silently replace a model version.

Bypass approval.

Ignore stale Ground-State conditions.

Continue after a fail-closed safety condition.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-011-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Agent SPEC Blueprint Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: DataContract | Section: 46. Conclusion | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentSpecEngine, PromptManager, ContractManager]

Within AI-ConneX, the Agent SPEC should be treated as the constitutional document of an industrial agent. It freezes the intended purpose, context, capabilities, permissions, constraints, tests and provenance into a versioned artifact. This gives the Agent Runtime a precise contract and gives industrialists, operations, engineering, security and governance teams a common object to review.

The architecture therefore becomes: Jane defines intent → Agent Builder compiles it → Agent SPEC establishes the contract → Policy and approval establish authority → Runtime enforces the contract → Tool Gateway controls side effects → Visualizer exposes the operational result. Data Studio and ML Studio remain authoritative sources for data lineage and evaluated models respectively.
